title: Gain on business real property: section 1231 netting
rule: Section 1231 covers gains and losses from selling, exchanging or involuntarily converting real or depreciable property used in a trade or business and held over one year, other than inventory or property held primarily for sale to customers. If a year's recognized section 1231 gains exceed its section 1231 losses, all are treated as long-term capital gains and losses; otherwise none is a capital gain or loss. A net section 1231 gain is ordinary income up to the non-recaptured net section 1231 losses of the five most recent preceding years. Unrecaptured section 1250 gain from a year's section 1231 dispositions cannot exceed that year's net section 1231 gain.
changeWatch: Amendments to section 1231(a), (b)(1) or (c), including the one-year holding period and the five-year look-back in 1231(c)(2), or to the limit on unrecaptured section 1250 gain in section 1(h)(6)(B).
